title: Existence of measurable versions of stochastic processes
summary: Let $(X, \mfA,P)$, $(Y, \mfB,Q)$ be two arbitrary probability spaces and $¶:=\{(\mfA,P_y):y\in{Y}\}$ be a regular conditional probability (rcp) on $\mfA$ with respect to $Q$. Denote by $R$ the skew product of $P$ and $Q$ determined by $¶$ on the product $σ$-algebra $\mfA\otimes\mfB$ and by $\wh{R}$ its completion. I prove that if $(X, \mfA,P)$ is separable in the Fréchet-Nikodým pseudo-metric, then the stochastic process $\{ξ_y:y\in{Y}\}$ has an equivalent measurable modification if and only if it is measurable with respect to a certain particular $σ$-algebra larger than $\mfA\otimes\mfB$.…
